title: Idea to product in 60 seconds
audience: Beginners who feel stuck choosing an idea
concept: Show how you filter a raw idea through three quick questions before spending any time on it.
hook: I almost wasted a month on a product nobody wanted. Here are the 3 questions that saved me.
structure: Question 1: Who exactly is this for? (3-20s)
Question 2: What problem does it solve? (20-38s)
Question 3: Would they pay for it today? (38-52s)
cta: Comment the idea you're testing and I'll tell you which question it fails.

title: The 10-minute idea sprint
audience: Aspiring creators with no idea yet
concept: Do a live timed brainstorm: set a 10-minute timer and write ideas from your own skills, frustrations and experience.
hook: Set a timer. In 10 minutes you will have more product ideas than most people find in a month.
structure: Show the timer and a blank page
Prompt 1: What do people ask you for help with?
Prompt 2: What did you have to learn the hard way?
Prompt 3: What do you wish existed?
Circle the top 2 and reveal your pick
cta: Save this and run your own sprint tonight.

title: Stop copying, start combining
audience: Creators who feel their niche is saturated
concept: Explain that originality is usually a combination: audience + format + angle.
hook: Your niche isn't too crowded. You're just using the same angle as everyone else.
cta: Drop your niche + audience combo below.

title: Who is it actually for?
concept: Walk through writing a one-sentence target audience statement.
hook: If your answer to 'who is this for?' is 'everyone', this video is for you.
cta: Write your sentence in the comments and I'll help tighten it.

title: Three places to find your first customers
concept: Show three free places to listen to your future audience: comments, forums and communities.
hook: You don't need followers to learn what your customers want. You need these 3 places.
structure: Place 1: Comment sections of bigger creators
cta: Follow for part 2: how to turn their words into your offer.

title: The comment goldmine
audience: Creators who struggle to find content topics
concept: Screen-record yourself scanning comments and turning them into video topics.
hook: Every comment section is a free content calendar. Watch this.
structure: Open a popular video in your niche
Turn each into a video title
Tell viewers to try it today
cta: Comment 'LIST' and I'll share my question-to-title formula.

title: Competitor research in 15 minutes
concept: Demonstrate a quick competitor review: offer, price, promise and gaps.
hook: Competitors aren't a threat. They're free market research. Here's how I study them.
structure: Note what they sell and for how much
Circle the gap you can fill
cta: Save this checklist before your next product idea.

title: What customers complain about
concept: Show how reading 3-star reviews reveals product opportunities.
hook: The best product ideas are hiding in 3-star reviews.
structure: Translate each into a product feature
cta: Which product would you improve? Tell me below.

title: Price check: how to choose a starter price
concept: Explain a simple method: compare to alternatives, time saved and perceived value.
hook: Pricing your first product isn't guesswork. Use this 3-step check.
structure: Step 2: How much time does it save?
Step 3: What feels fair for a beginner?
Pick a price and commit to testing it
cta: Share your price range and I'll tell you what I'd test.

title: Build your first product in a weekend
concept: Outline a realistic weekend plan for a small digital product.
hook: You can make a small digital product this weekend. Not a perfect one. A useful one.
cta: Start tonight and tell me what you're making.

title: The one-page PDF trick
audience: Creators who want a lead magnet
concept: Show how to turn one piece of advice into a useful one-page PDF.
hook: Your first digital product can be one page long.
structure: Design it in a free tool
cta: Comment 'PAGE' for my one-page layout idea.

title: Test your product before finishing it
concept: Show how to share a draft with 3 people and collect useful feedback.
hook: Don't finish your product. Test it first.
structure: Share a rough draft with 3 people
cta: Want my 3 feedback questions? Follow and comment 'FEEDBACK'.

title: Brand in 3 choices
concept: Explain the three decisions that make a brand feel professional: colours, fonts and tone.
hook: You don't need a designer. You need three decisions.
structure: Pick two colours and a neutral
Pick one heading and one body font
Write 3 words that describe your voice
cta: Show me your brand colours below.

title: Fix amateur-looking posts
concept: Show a messy post, then fix spacing, hierarchy and contrast.
hook: This post looks amateur. Three small fixes make it look pro.
cta: Send me a post you'd like me to fix.

title: Name your brand without panic
concept: Give a quick naming process: keywords, feelings and a short list test.
hook: Choosing a brand name took me hours. This method takes 10 minutes.
structure: Check availability and keep the best two
cta: Which of these would you pick? Comment your favourite.

title: Your sales page in five blocks
concept: Break a sales page into headline, problem, solution, proof/inclusions and call to action.
hook: A sales page only needs five blocks. Here they are.
structure: Call to action: one next step
cta: Save this and use it for your own page.

title: Words that make buyers hesitate
concept: Show common vague phrases and replace them with specific statements.
hook: If your sales page says 'amazing quality', fix this first.
structure: Do it again with a second sentence
cta: Drop a sentence and I'll rewrite it.

title: Honest FAQs build trust
concept: Explain that answering real objections increases confidence.
hook: The most trustworthy thing on your sales page is an honest FAQ.
structure: Show what you include and exclude
Link to refund and delivery info
cta: Which question would stop you from buying? Tell me.

title: Hooks that stop the scroll
concept: Present three hook styles: question, bold claim and mini-story.
hook: You have two seconds. Here are three hooks that earn them.
structure: Rewrite the weak opening with one of them
cta: Comment which hook you'll try first.

title: Repurpose one idea five ways
concept: Show one idea turned into a video, carousel, story, caption and email.
hook: One idea. Five posts. Zero burnout.
structure: Turn it into a short video
Turn it into stories and a caption
Add a short email or note
cta: Which format will you try first?

title: The simple weekly content plan
concept: Show a basic weekly rhythm: 3 educational, 1 personal, 1 offer post.
hook: Posting every day isn't the plan. This is.
cta: Want the planner? Look at the link in my bio.

title: Post → profile → product
audience: Creators with views but no sales
concept: Explain the journey from video to profile to offer and how to make each step clear.
hook: Lots of views but no sales? Check these three steps.
structure: Does the video promise one thing?
Does the profile explain who you help?
Is the link easy to find?
Does the page match the video?
cta: Tell me which step is weakest for you.

title: A bio that converts
concept: Rewrite a vague bio into: who you help + result + next step.
hook: Your bio has about 3 seconds to explain why someone should follow.
cta: Paste your bio below and I'll improve it.

title: What I track every week
concept: Show 4 simple metrics: views, saves, shares and link clicks.
hook: Ignore most analytics. Track these four numbers.
cta: Save this and check them every Sunday.

title: Money basics for creators
concept: Introduce revenue vs profit and why tracking costs matters.
hook: Revenue isn't what you keep. This simple example shows why.
structure: Explain why to track it monthly
cta: Want a simple money tracker? Comment 'TRACK'.

title: Set aside money for taxes
concept: Remind viewers that income may be taxable and that they should check local rules.
hook: Selling online? Don't forget this boring but important step.
structure: Set aside a portion of each sale
cta: Follow for more money basics. This is general information, not tax advice.

title: My first 30-day plan
concept: Outline a realistic 30-day plan: week 1 idea, week 2 build, week 3 launch, week 4 learn.
hook: If I were starting from zero, here's my exact 30-day plan.
cta: Comment 'PLAN' to get the weekly checklist.

title: Content batching Sunday
concept: Show a one-hour batching session: ideas, scripts, filming and scheduling.
hook: One hour on Sunday saves me five hours during the week.
structure: Write short scripts or bullet points
cta: Try this Sunday and report back.

title: Realistic expectations
concept: Honest video: growth takes time; focus on skills, consistency and feedback.
hook: Nobody tells beginners this, so I will.
structure: What you can control: posting, learning, improving
What you can't: algorithms and timing
cta: Share one thing you learned this week.

title: Your next 3 videos
concept: Close the series by helping viewers choose their next three videos from their own audience questions.
hook: Stuck on what to post? Do this and you'll know your next three videos.
structure: Open your last 10 comments or DMs
cta: Comment your first hook and I'll give feedback.
